data.title: Anogenital warts — viva
data.summary: Sexually transmitted infections · 10 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Anogenital warts** (Sexually transmitted infections)_

**Q1. What are anogenital warts and their HPV types?**
- Benign epithelial proliferations of anogenital skin/mucosa caused by HPV — mainly low-risk types 6 and 11 (~90%); high-risk 16, 18, 31, 33 cause intraepithelial neoplasia and carcinoma

**Q2. Clinical types?**
- Condylomata acuminata (cauliflower/acuminate), papular (dome-shaped, keratinised skin), keratotic, flat/macular (mucosal — visible with acetowhitening), giant condyloma of Buschke–Löwenstein (verrucous carcinoma), intraepithelial neoplasia (bowenoid papulosis, Bowen disease)

**Q3. How are they transmitted? Significance in a child?**
- Sexual contact (most), perinatal (maternal), autoinoculation/heteroinoculation from hand warts, fomites (rare)
- In children consider sexual abuse, especially >3 years — sensitive evaluation

**Q4. Condyloma acuminata vs condyloma lata?**
- Lata (secondary syphilis): flat-topped, moist, broad-based, grey-white, highly infectious, dark-ground positive, generalised lymphadenopathy
- Acuminata: pink, dry, papillomatous, narrow base (paper can be passed under it), DGI negative

**Q5. Differential diagnosis?**
- Pearly penile papules, Fordyce spots, vestibular papillae, molluscum, seborrhoeic keratosis, skin tags, condyloma lata, bowenoid papulosis, lichen planus, scabies nodules, SCC

**Q6. Histopathology?**
- Acanthosis, papillomatosis, koilocytes (perinuclear halo with raisinoid nuclei) in upper layers, parakeratosis

**Q7. What is the acetowhite test?**
- 3–5% acetic acid for 3–5 min turns HPV-infected epithelium white — helps identify subclinical lesions, but non-specific

**Q8. Treatment of external genital warts?**
- Patient-applied: podophyllotoxin 0.5% solution/0.15% cream (3 days on, 4 off, up to 4 cycles), imiquimod 5% cream thrice weekly up to 16 weeks, sinecatechins 15% ointment three times daily up to 16 weeks
- Provider-administered: cryotherapy (preferred in pregnancy), TCA 80–90%, podophyllin 10–25% (wash off in 1–4 h), electrocautery, surgical excision, CO2 laser
- Special situations: intralesional interferon, 5-FU, cidofovir, immunotherapy

**Q9. Warts in pregnancy?**
- Grow rapidly and may bleed/obstruct labour; podophyllin, podophyllotoxin and imiquimod avoided; cryotherapy/TCA/excision; caesarean only for obstruction or bleeding; risk of juvenile laryngeal papillomatosis in baby

**Q10. Is a vaccine available?**
- Yes — quadrivalent (6, 11, 16, 18) and 9-valent HPV vaccines prevent anogenital warts; bivalent (16, 18) does not prevent warts

## Quick spotter facts
- Cauliflower-like papillomatous growths on the prepuce — condylomata acuminata

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Long case — Anogenital warts); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.131. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
